Gate definition

What do the columns and symbols mean?

This page is the legend of the Tableaux tooling plan, and every other view links here. It shows the project-wide legend, then the legend for one task, e9c6. It shows all ten gates; with a window or a column list it shows those gates only.

The page opens at detail for the owner, as for every role with an email in the project. An observer, and every reader of a static export, arrives with each row folded to its symbol, name and key. Provenance stays folded until the reader asks.

Reasons

A reason explains a state, and its symbol stands beside the state's symbol.
SymbolReason, with its synopsis
🪫
overloaded

⛔

review

The work waits for its reviewer

The method reserves review: the contributor has handed the next junction's work to its reviewer, and the queue lists the review as owed. 👓 beside a state says the work waits for its reviewer; 👀 in a cell says a reviewer accepts the work there.

Junction marks

A junction is the meeting of a task and a gate, one cell of a tableau. The marks belong to the method, not to this project.
MarkMeaning, with the junction that shows it
🧑

—

Not applicable; the entry exempts the task from the gate

Detail for one task

The task parameter adds one fact to each gate: how the junction of that task at the gate expands the criteria. This section takes e9c6 Abstract views, a task under the Method branch bc63. The states, reasons and junction marks do not change with the task. A link from the task, queue or context page names the task; this page has no task chooser of its own.

e9c6 Abstract views: six gates apply, four do not, and no junction states a reference
